plan.notes: Source: official St. John's University program page for the BS in Computer Science (https://www.stjohns.edu/academics/programs/computer-science-bachelor-science), transcribed 2026-09-30. Degree name verified: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (BS, not BA), 120 credits, housed in the Lesley H. and William L. Collins College of Professional Studies; program is ABET-accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission. Catalog year 2025-2027: the current Undergraduate Bulletin cycle per https://www.stjohns.edu/academics/academic-resources-and-programs/bulletins/undergraduate-bulletin (the program page itself carries no bulletin-year stamp). Transcription method: the page's 'Computer Science Recommended Course Sequence' (Semesters 1-8) was transcribed term by term; course titles and credits come from the same page's Major Area (36 cr), Additional Area (9 cr), Common Core (39 cr), Other Liberal Arts (32-34 cr: ECO 3 + Math 15 + advanced Math 6 + Science 8-10), and Free Electives (6 cr) tables. No courses, credits, or prerequisites were invented. Caveats: (1) The sequence prints 15 credits per term (8 x 15 = 120). The catalog's lab-science options carry 4 credits (BIO 1000/2000 with lab) or 5 credits (PHY 1610/1620 or CHE 1210/1220 with lab+recitation), so a student taking those sciences carries 16-17 credits in Semesters 3-4; the science slots are framed at 3 credits here to match the sequence's published 15-credit term totals, with the catalog credits documented in each choice_note. (2) The requirement breakdown sums to 122-124 credits against the 120-credit degree minimum; the plan follows the sequence's own published total of 120. (3) The sequence's advanced-math list (MTH 1011/1012/1015/1016/1017/1019) omits MTH 1018 Differential Equations, which the requirements table also lists; documented in the Semester 5 choice_note. (4) CUS 1166 Software Engineering is listed in both Semester 7 and Semester 8 ('if not taken in semester 7'); it is modeled once, in Semester 7, since the 36-credit major requires it exactly once. (5) The sequence's Semester 1 'First Year Seminar' is fulfilled by DNY 1000C Discover New York, the university's first-year seminar and a listed common-core course. (6) Semester 2 'Theology course' and 'Philosophy course' are fulfilled by THE 1000C and PHI 1000C, the designated first courses in the published core table (this also sequences the later THE 1040-series, PHI 3000C, and PHI 1020-series requirements correctly). (7) Grade gates per the program page: a minimum grade of C in CUS 1116 is required to continue to CUS 1126, and a minimum grade of C in CUS 1126 is required to continue to upper-level CUS courses; upper-level CUS prereqs of CUS 1126 are corroborated by the CCPS bulletin course descriptions (e.g., 'Prerequisite: CUS 1126' for CUS 1161/1162). (8) The plan assumes calculus readiness; students not ready for MTH 1009 begin with preparatory math as advised. (9) Prereq codes are plain code strings; every prereq names an in-plan course code (choice-slot prereqs point at the choice slot's own code, e.g. SCI 10XX-2 -> SCI 10XX-1).
